business_problem: Baseten needed to offer customers a cloud inference platform that could scale from sporadic traffic to high-volume real-time demand while keeping cold starts, infrastructure costs, and operational complexity low.
solution_summary: Baseten built its managed inference platform on NVIDIA GPU instances in AWS and paired that compute layer with NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM to speed up large-model serving. Customers can bring their own models or deploy pretrained ones through Baseten's open-source Truss framework, which packages the models and routes them onto autoscaling GPU infrastructure. NVIDIA A100 and A10-class instances supply the accelerated runtime, while TensorRT-LLM provides optimizations such as tensor parallelism to improve LLM throughput and cost efficiency. NVIDIA AI Enterprise gives Baseten access to the production-grade TensorRT-LLM stack, and the platform's autoscaling controls adjust replicas as traffic changes. Together, those pieces let Baseten turn model deployment into an on-demand service with fast startup times and less manual infrastructure tuning.

data_flow: Customers package models with Truss or choose pretrained ones, Baseten deploys them onto autoscaling EC2 GPU instances, TensorRT-LLM serves the optimized inference path on A100 or A10 hardware, and results are returned through the managed platform as traffic expands or contracts.
business_outcome: Baseten reduced cold starts from up to five minutes to roughly 5-10 seconds, delivered 30-60x faster startup behavior, and boosted one customer's LLM inference performance by 2x while keeping the platform elastic enough for real-time workloads.
